title: Open questions in knot polynomials and surgery

items.title: Unique Laurent decomposition for the Jones–Vassiliev basis
items.statement:
Let $x$ be an invertible indeterminate and put $p=x-x^{-1}$. Every Laurent
polynomial $P(x)\in\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]$ has a unique expression
$$P(x)=a(p)+b(p)x$$
with $a,b\in\mathbb Z[p]$, where $\mathbb Z[p]$ is the ring of finite
integer-coefficient polynomials in the indeterminate $p$.
items.strategy: Identify Z[p][X]/(X²−pX−1) with Z[x,x⁻¹]; monic division gives the unique degree-at-most-one representative.

references.title: Avishy Carmi and Eliahu Cohen, On trivial Jones–Vassiliev polynomials, arXiv:2606.22410v1, Lemma 3.1 and Appendix B.1

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the Laurent-polynomial quotient and monic-remainder argument use only finite algebraic constructions.

items.title: Jones–Vassiliev coefficient vectors
items.statement:
Assume full AC for the library Jones invariant. An oriented link is a finite
disjoint union of oriented smooth circles embedded in $S^3$, considered up to
ambient isotopy; an oriented classical knot is the one-component case. For an
oriented link $L\subset S^3$, let $V_L(x)\in\mathbb Z[x^{\pm1}]$ be the
library-normalized Jones polynomial, with $V_U(x)=1$ for the unknot $U$;
write $V_K$ for its value on a knot $K$. Here $x=t^{1/2}$ in the library
convention $t=A^{-4}$, so an oriented skein triple satisfies
$$x^{-2}V_{L_+}(x)-x^2V_{L_-}(x)=(x-x^{-1})V_{L_0}(x).$$
Set $p=x-x^{-1}$. By the unique Laurent decomposition, write
$$V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)p^q,$$
where $a_q(K),b_q(K)\in\mathbb Z$ and only finitely many are nonzero. The
**Jones–Vassiliev coefficient vector of order $q$** is
$$f_q(K):=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T},$$
and $c_q(K):=a_q(K)+b_q(K)$. This is the algebraic coefficient-vector
definition used by Carmi and Cohen. The claim that the coordinates of $f_q$
are finite-type invariants of order at most $q$ is a separate theorem and is
not part of this definition.
items.strategy: Define the coefficient vectors from the proved unique Laurent decomposition and the normalized library Jones polynomial.

references.title: Avishy Carmi and Eliahu Cohen, On trivial Jones–Vassiliev polynomials, arXiv:2606.22410v1, §1.3 and Lemma 3.1
Louis H. Kauffman, Combinatorial Knot Theory and the Jones Polynomial, arXiv:2204.12104v2, §2
Dror Bar-Natan and Alexander Stoimenow, The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants, arXiv:q-alg/9702009v1, §1.1

items.axiom_use: Full AC is required by the library Jones-invariance supplier. The coefficient decomposition itself is a finite, choice-free algebraic construction.

items.title: Jones polynomial unknot-detection status
items.statement:
## Historical question

Assume full AC for the library Jones invariant and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for
the crossing number. A classical knot is a smooth embedding
$S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ considered up to ambient isotopy; $U$ is the unknot
represented by a crossing-free circle, and “nontrivial” means it is not
ambient isotopic to $U$. A regular diagram is a generic plane projection with only
transverse double points, each marked with over/under information. Let $c(K)$
be the least crossing count among regular diagrams representing $K$. Let
$V_K(x)$ be the library-normalized Jones polynomial with $V_U(x)=1$, where
$x=t^{1/2}$ and $t=A^{-4}$. Set $p=x-x^{-1}$ and write the unique expansion
$$V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)p^q,$$
where the integer coefficients have finite support; set
$f_q(K)=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T}$. The historical Jones
unknot-detection question is whether $V_K(x)=1$ implies $K=U$.

## Status

Roberts's 1999 notes record the implication as a conjecture. Carmi and Cohen's
arXiv:2606.22410v1, submitted on 2026-06-21, claims that every nontrivial
classical knot has a nonzero coefficient vector $f_q(K)$ for some integer
$q$ with $2\le q\le3c(K)$, and claims $V_K(x)=1\Rightarrow K=U$. This
scaffold has read the stated result and the paper's proof route but has not
independently validated the claimed proof; it asserts neither proof acceptance
nor a definitive current open status.

The source's machine argument still requires an independent diagram-level
audit of Proposition 5.12, particularly its exceptional-state collapse,
smoothing proxy, and two-machine locality. Its numerical estimate
$B_{\rm aux}\le B_{\rm host}+12$ is consistent with the stated overhead
$\kappa_{\rm mach}=11$: the argument uses the next layer $r+1$ after
$r>B_{\rm host}+11$. This arithmetic check does not verify the geometric
reductions. No Jones-detection theorem is registered by this scaffold.
items.strategy: Record the historical conjecture, dated source claim, exact unresolved verification scope, and non-acceptance status without using the claim as a supplier.

references.title: Avishy Carmi and Eliahu Cohen, On trivial Jones–Vassiliev polynomials, arXiv:2606.22410v1, submitted 2026-06-21
Louis H. Kauffman, Combinatorial Knot Theory and the Jones Polynomial, arXiv:2204.12104v2, §2

items.axiom_use: The library Jones normalization uses full AC; the crossing-number convention declares AC_omega. The finite-type terminology concerns unframed knots, whose singular-knot definition is choice-free.

items.title: The unknot defeats a universal coefficient-bound extension
items.statement:
Assume full AC for the Jones invariant and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for $c(K)$.
A classical knot is a smooth embedding $S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ considered
up to ambient isotopy. A regular diagram is a generic plane projection with
only transverse double points, each marked with over/under information. The
false universal extension is: for every classical knot $K$, including the
unknot, there is an integer $q$ with $2\le q\le3c(K)$ and
$f_q(K)\ne(0,0)^{\mathsf T}$. Here $V_K(x)$ is the normalized library Jones
polynomial with $V_U(x)=1$, $f_q(K)=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T}$ is defined by
the unique expansion $V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)(x-x^{-1})^q$, and
$c(K)$ is the least crossing number of a regular diagram of $K$.

The boundary input is the unknot $U$, represented by the crossing-free circle:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9,line cap=round]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (0.55);
  \node at (0,-0.9) {$U$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
items.strategy: Use the unknot's normalized constant Jones polynomial and zero crossing number to refute the universal extension to all knots.

references.title: Avishy Carmi and Eliahu Cohen, On trivial Jones–Vassiliev polynomials, arXiv:2606.22410v1, submitted 2026-06-21

items.axiom_use: Full AC is used through the Jones-invariance supplier; AC_omega is the declared crossing-number hypothesis. The unknot expansion and empty coefficient range are choice-free.
